## Request
TransDigm Group Incorporated, as of 2024-09-30; pathway: distressed_restructuring. Scope is the consolidated FY2024 financial foundation, comparison with FY2023, debt reconciliation and separately identified subsequent financing and distribution events, not a finding of actual distress.

## Findings

### Bottom line
TransDigm's improving cash generation does not establish deleveraging: gross leverage increased, and the already-declared October distribution materially reduces the cash offset protecting creditors. The financial statements support a usable annual baseline, but not a covenant-capacity or recovery conclusion.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 120–123; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 170; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3

Reported-EBITDA gross leverage rose from 6.27x to 6.53x even as cash-interest coverage improved from 2.71x to 3.29x. Year-end net debt of USD 18,619 million and net leverage of 4.88x become USD 22,967 million and 6.02x after the 2024-10-18 distribution, holding earnings and all other movements constant. This is a transaction-only illustration, not a later balance sheet. Stronger operating cash flow is the principal counterweight; retaining it rather than distributing or reinvesting it would make the deleveraging argument more persuasive.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 71–72; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 123; TDG_FY2024_annual-report_SEC-PDF_0001260221-25-000008_a841225transdigmgroupbookm.pdf, page 48; calculation C3; calculation C4

### Causal downside and monitoring
A slowdown in aftermarket activity or aircraft production would first pressure segment sales and inventory conversion. If collections weakened while acquired businesses absorbed integration cash, operating cash generation would fall before the distant term and note maturities became the immediate constraint. The October distribution leaves less cash to absorb that operational shortfall; the first financing pressure would therefore be the receivables facility and revolver dependence, not an assumed imminent bond maturity. Observable warnings are renewed receivable and inventory absorption, cash paid catching up with accrued interest, failure to renew receivables financing, and rising revolver usage.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 50, 56–57, 62, 71, 123 and 153; TDG_FY2024_annual-report_SEC-PDF_0001260221-25-000008_a841225transdigmgroupbookm.pdf, pages 47–48

The strongest challenge to that downside is the documented improvement in segment margins and actual operating cash generation, together with the extended financing maturities and reported covenant compliance. It would outweigh concern over the cash distribution if cash were subsequently retained and collections remained sound. Conversely, recurring debt-funded distributions or acquisitions would weaken the inference that operating improvement will accrue to creditors. No stress magnitude, default date or covenant headroom is established here.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 50, 53–56, 62 and 123

### Limitations
The annual filing was published after the requested reporting date; the analysis is a reporting-date reconstruction, not a contemporaneously available investment view. The annual shareholder report supplies more precise October event dates and remains a separate document version. The event-only calculations do not include later operating cash flows or later purchase-price settlements and must not be read as actual later net debt. No independent external corroboration or visual inspection is claimed.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 120; TDG_FY2024_annual-report_SEC-PDF_0001260221-25-000008_a841225transdigmgroupbookm.pdf, pages 47–48

Consolidated cash and earnings do not establish access to cash within the actual obligor and guarantor group. Summary payment rankings do not resolve collateral priority, competing liens or restrictions on transfers from non-guarantors. Covenant capacity, enforceable waterfall and numerical recoveries remain restricted pending operative agreements and claim-level allocation evidence.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 57, 59, 61–62, 146 and 153; Source readiness (CP-0)

## Gaps

High severity: controlling credit agreements, indentures, guarantee and collateral schedules and intercreditor terms are absent. The summary rank descriptions support a partial descriptive stack only; securitization, finance leases and government advances are excluded from relative-ranking subtotals because their relative priority is not established. Obtain the operative documents and obligor-level balances to establish enforceable priority, cash accessibility, covenant capacity and recoveries.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 57, 61–62, 145–146 and 153; Source readiness (CP-0)

Medium severity: FFO, FFO interest cover, separate gross interest expense and separate interest income are not established. Cash interest paid net is usable for historical coverage but not a substitute for forward debt service. Obtain the gross interest schedule, hedge settlements and a defined FFO reconciliation before using those measures. The same restriction applies to both annual periods.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 71, 121 and 123

Medium severity: maintenance and growth capex, unlevered cash-tax treatment, separately identified disposal cash proceeds and a comprehensive exceptional subtotal are not established for either year. Total-capex levered FCF remains usable; a maintenance-only cash yield, unlevered FCF or pure recurring earnings conclusion does not. Obtain the underlying expenditure, disposal and adjustment schedules. Stock compensation is disclosed both as stock-option equity expense and as a broader stock-and-deferred-compensation add-back; the broader amount must not be relabelled as pure stock compensation.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 71 and 122–123

Medium severity: the calculated broad operating asset and liability cash movement and the management EBITDA-bridge reversal have different scopes, and their difference is not fully decomposed. Obtain the bridge detail before treating either as a clean measure of recurring working-capital absorption. Their distinct reported and calculated identities have been retained rather than forced to agree.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 71 and 123; calculation C7

Low severity: several source dashes are retained as missing quantities rather than converted to zero. These include discontinued operations, some disposal and retirement-plan cash-flow adjustments, repurchases, revolver repayments, prior-year securitization proceeds and prior-year dividends payable. Restricted cash, short-term investments, a separate senior unsecured debt subtotal and pension liabilities are not separately established in this extraction. These gaps do not invalidate reported statement totals, but prevent asserting the absence of the omitted items or building a fully component-level liability model. Obtain the relevant note detail where such conclusions are required.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 120–123 and 145

Low severity: individual term-tranche carrying values, separate revolver drawn and carrying balances, revolving-facility floor terms, securitization annual amortisation terms and the contractual rates, security, priority and annual repayment terms of government advances and finance leases are not fully established. Finance lease future cash payments include interest and are not annual principal repayments. Obtain instrument-level schedules before allocating financing costs, modelling cash service or extending the partial rank analysis. The aggregate term facility and all disclosed instrument carrying values already reconcile to reported debt without estimating tranche-level values.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 59–62, 144–145, 152–153 and 172; calculation C10

Low severity: separately stated corporate revenue eliminations, comparable non-financial operating series, prior-year rank subtotals and additional interim constructions were not established here. Segment revenue and segment adjusted earnings nevertheless reconcile to the selected annual consolidated measures. The supplied interim and later filings remain separate evidence; matched-period extraction is required before drawing interim trend conclusions, and later operating cash flows or purchase-price settlements must not be included silently in the event-only October illustration.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 49–50; Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C11

Low severity: no strict publication cutoff was supplied, and the annual shareholder report publication date is not stated in the inspected evidence. The annual filing and more precise subsequent-event dates support a retrospective reporting-date analysis only. A complete later-event ledger, including later operations, later purchase-price settlements and any later repurchases, is not established by the targeted annual review. Establish the historical information cutoff or reconcile a separately dated later balance sheet before using these figures for a contemporaneous decision.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); TDG_FY2024_annual-report_SEC-PDF_0001260221-25-000008_a841225transdigmgroupbookm.pdf, pages 47–48
